title: Welcome-flow revenue quietly collapsed
instructions: Someone on the exec team pulled up welcome-series numbers for the board deck and revenue is way down from where it was a year ago. I pulled the flow and the emails look fine to me — same copy, same cadence, people are still opening and clicking. Can you dig in and tell us what's actually going on and what it's costing us? Need something I can forward as-is.

criteria.text: Identifies the dead/expired meridian-travel.com domain in the welcome-flow links as the root cause of the conversion collapse.

Notes that click rates on the welcome emails stayed healthy while post-click sessions and conversions collapsed, and does not misattribute the drop to creative fatigue, subject lines, or deliverability/inboxing issues.
States timing consistent with the March 2, 2026 domain migration and the July 1, 2026 old-domain redirect expiry.
States the pre-migration welcome-flow conversion rate, reconciling with the answer-key value within tolerance.

regexes: (?:pre-migration|before the migration|prior to the migration|through Feb(?:ruary)? 2026|historically ran at)[\s\S]{0,80}?(0\.0\d{1,3})
extract.hint: the welcome-flow conversion rate before the March 2026 domain migration, as a decimal fraction (e.g. 0.041)

criteria.text: States the post-migration welcome-flow conversion rate, reconciling with the answer-key value within tolerance.

regexes: (?:post-migration|since the migration|now converting at|has fallen to|has collapsed to|dropped to|down to)[\s\S]{0,80}?(0\.0\d{1,3})
extract.hint: the welcome-flow conversion rate after the March 2026 domain migration / July 1 redirect expiry, as a decimal fraction (e.g. 0.009)

criteria.text: Proposes both an immediate fix (repoint the welcome-flow links to the live domain) and a prevention practice (link/domain monitoring).
Notes that the affected cohort could be re-mailed with working links.
